claim: Jag2 is the first Notch ligand detected in the airway epithelium, initially restricted to the trachea at around E12.0
source: By in situ hybridization (ISH) analysis none of these ligands were detectable in the airway epithelium prior to or at E11.5 (not shown). However, at around E12.0 evidence of Jag2 epithelial signals in the developing trachea made it the first of all Notch ligands to be induced in the differentiation program of airways (Figure 1A).
evidence: Supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1A and described in the text

claim: Jag2 expression progresses in a proximal-to-distal fashion in developing airways
source: Expression progressed in a proximal-to-distal fashion; at E12.5 low level signals were detected in the epithelium of extrapulmonary but not intrapulmonary airways.
evidence: Based on in situ hybridization observations at different developmental stages

claim: Jag2 detection in epithelial progenitors of the trachea and extrapulmonary airways coincides with the onset of Notch activation and appearance of the secretory cell marker Scgb3a2
source: Notably, the Jag2 detection in epithelial progenitors of the trachea and extrapulmonary airways coincided with the previously reported onset of Notch activation and appearance of the secretory cell marker Scgb3a2 locally (Guha et al., 2012).
evidence: Temporal correlation with previously published findings cited in the manuscript

claim: No epithelial Jag1 could be detected in airways at E12.0-E12.5 stages
source: No epithelial Jag1 could be detected anywhere in airways at these stages, although clearly present in vascular structures (Figure 1C).
evidence: Based on in situ hybridization analysis shown in Figure 1C

claim: Expression of Ascl1, which marks PNEC precursors, was first found around E13-13.5 in large intrapulmonary airways
source: Indeed, expression of Ascl1, which marks PNEC precursors, was first found ~E13-13.5 in large intrapulmonary airways and both Dll1 and Dll4 were then subsequently expressed in these precursors (Figure 1E,D).
evidence: Based on in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1D and 1E

claim: Dll1 and Dll4 are subsequently expressed in PNEC precursors after Ascl1 expression
source: Indeed, expression of Ascl1, which marks PNEC precursors, was first found ~E13-13.5 in large intrapulmonary airways and both Dll1 and Dll4 were then subsequently expressed in these precursors (Figure 1E,D).
evidence: Based on in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1D and 1E

claim: By E13.5-E14.5 strong Jag2 epithelial signals were seen throughout the trachea and main bronchi, in contrast to Jag1, nearly undetected at these sites
source: By E13.5-E14.5 strong Jag2 epithelial signals were seen throughout the trachea and main bronchi, in contrast to Jag1, nearly undetected at these sites (Figure 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Based on in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 1

claim: At E14.5 NEBs and PNECs were sharply demarcated by Ascl1, and Dll1 and Dll4 transcripts became prominently expressed in NEBs
source: At E14.5 NEBs and PNECs were sharply demarcated by Ascl1, and Dll1 and Dll4 transcripts became prominently expressed in NEBs (Figure 1E–F).
evidence: Based on in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1E-F

claim: Clusters of cells adjacent to NEBs at E14.5 are collectively marked by expression of Upk3a, SSEA1, Scgb3a2 and low levels of Cyp2f2 and CC10
source: This was accompanied by the appearance of clusters of cells adjacent to NEBs, collectively marked by expression of the uroplakin Upk3a, the cell surface stem cell (secretory) marker SSEA1, the secretoglobin Scgb3a2 and low levels of the cytochrome gene Cyp2f2 and CC10.
evidence: Based on marker expression analysis

claim: The pattern of marker expression is consistent with the initiation of a Notch-dependent program of secretory cells in the NEB microenvironment
source: The pattern was consistent with the initiation of a Notch-dependent program of secretory cells in the NEB microenvironment (Guha et al., 2012 and described later).
evidence: Interpretation of marker expression patterns with reference to previous work

claim: Expression of the secretory marker Scgb3a2 was reduced by 86.2% in Jag1cnull mutants
source: Expression of the secretory markers Scgb3a2 and Scgb1a1 (encoding CC10) were reduced by 86.2% (p=5×10−12) and 85.6% (p=0.0001), respectively in Jag1cnull mutants, but only by 25.9% (p=0.015) and 34.4% (p=0.019), respectively in Jag2cnull mutants.
evidence: Based on qPCR analysis of E18.5 lung homogenates shown in Figure 2A

claim: Expression of the secretory marker Scgb1a1 (CC10) was reduced by 85.6% in Jag1cnull mutants
source: Expression of the secretory markers Scgb3a2 and Scgb1a1 (encoding CC10) were reduced by 86.2% (p=5×10−12) and 85.6% (p=0.0001), respectively in Jag1cnull mutants, but only by 25.9% (p=0.015) and 34.4% (p=0.019), respectively in Jag2cnull mutants.
evidence: Based on qPCR analysis of E18.5 lung homogenates shown in Figure 2A

claim: Expression of Scgb3a2 was reduced by 25.9% in Jag2cnull mutants
source: Expression of the secretory markers Scgb3a2 and Scgb1a1 (encoding CC10) were reduced by 86.2% (p=5×10−12) and 85.6% (p=0.0001), respectively in Jag1cnull mutants, but only by 25.9% (p=0.015) and 34.4% (p=0.019), respectively in Jag2cnull mutants.
evidence: Based on qPCR analysis of E18.5 lung homogenates shown in Figure 2A

claim: Expression of Scgb1a1 was reduced by 34.4% in Jag2cnull mutants
source: Expression of the secretory markers Scgb3a2 and Scgb1a1 (encoding CC10) were reduced by 86.2% (p=5×10−12) and 85.6% (p=0.0001), respectively in Jag1cnull mutants, but only by 25.9% (p=0.015) and 34.4% (p=0.019), respectively in Jag2cnull mutants.
evidence: Based on qPCR analysis of E18.5 lung homogenates shown in Figure 2A

claim: Foxj1 expression increased by 183% in Jag1cnull mutants
source: These changes were accompanied by a significant increase in Foxj1 expression in Jag1cnull (183% increase, p=0.0006) but not in Jag2cnull (13% reduction, p=0.501) mutants.
evidence: Based on qPCR analysis of E18.5 lung homogenates shown in Figure 2A

claim: Foxj1 expression showed a 13% reduction in Jag2cnull mutants, which was not statistically significant
source: These changes were accompanied by a significant increase in Foxj1 expression in Jag1cnull (183% increase, p=0.0006) but not in Jag2cnull (13% reduction, p=0.501) mutants.
evidence: Based on qPCR analysis of E18.5 lung homogenates shown in Figure 2A

claim: The differentiation program of intrapulmonary airways was more severely affected in Jag1cnull than in Jag2cnull mutants
source: Thus, the differentiation program of intrapulmonary airways was more severely affected in Jag1cnull than in Jag2cnull mutants.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from comparing qPCR data between Jag1cnull and Jag2cnull mutants

claim: Double Jag1cnull; Jag2cnull mutants showed Scgb3a2 and Scgb1a1 nearly abolished
source: These mutants showed Scgb3a2 and Scgb1a1 nearly abolished and an increase in Foxj1 similar to that found in Jag1cnull.
evidence: Based on qPCR analysis of E18.5 lung homogenates shown in Figure 2A

claim: Double Jag1cnull; Jag2cnull mutants showed an increase in Foxj1 similar to that found in Jag1cnull
source: These mutants showed Scgb3a2 and Scgb1a1 nearly abolished and an increase in Foxj1 similar to that found in Jag1cnull.
evidence: Based on qPCR analysis of E18.5 lung homogenates shown in Figure 2A

claim: Airway progenitors are largely dependent on Jag ligands to initiate secretory cell differentiation
source: Altogether these results indicated that airway progenitors are largely dependent on Jag ligands to initiate secretory cell differentiation.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from the combined analysis of single and double Jag mutants

claim: Morphometric analysis showed no significant change in the number of Foxj1+ cells in Jag2cnull airways relative to control
source: Morphometric analysis showed no significant change in the number of Foxj1+ cells in Jag2cnull airways relative to control (p=0.164), in contrast to the ~2.5 fold increase in these cells in Jag1cnull mutants (p=4.17×10−7) (Figure 2C).
evidence: Based on morphometric analysis shown in Figure 2C

claim: Jag1cnull mutants showed approximately 2.5 fold increase in Foxj1+ cells
source: Morphometric analysis showed no significant change in the number of Foxj1+ cells in Jag2cnull airways relative to control (p=0.164), in contrast to the ~2.5 fold increase in these cells in Jag1cnull mutants (p=4.17×10−7) (Figure 2C).
evidence: Based on morphometric analysis shown in Figure 2C

claim: Jag2 expression in the trachea and extrapulmonary airways continued to be robust at E14.5-E18.5 stages while remaining weak and scattered in intrapulmonary bronchial epithelia
source: Interestingly, ISH of E14.5- E18.5 WT lungs showed that Jag2 expression in the trachea and extrapulmonary airways continued to be robust at later stages while remaining weak and scattered in intrapulmonary bronchial epithelia.
evidence: Based on in situ hybridization analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1

claim: Jag1 expression was progressively stronger in the intrapulmonary airway epithelium from E15.5 onwards
source: By contrast, Jag1 expression was progressively stronger in the intrapulmonary airway epithelium from E15.5 onwards and by E18.5 expression extended to the distal bronchioles.
evidence: Based on in situ hybridization analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1

claim: Jag1 is localized in multiciliated cells
source: Double ISH-immunohistochemistry for Foxj1 confirmed our previous report of Jag1 localization in multiciliated cells (Tsao et al., 2009).
evidence: Based on double ISH-immunohistochemistry data and previous publication

claim: Jag1 is the predominant ligand in intrapulmonary airways mediating secretory vs. multiciliated cell fate choice during differentiation
source: Thus, our data suggested that Jag1 is the predominant ligand in intrapulmonary airways mediating secretory vs. multiciliated cell fate choice during differentiation.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from expression pattern analysis and mutant phenotypes

claim: In Jag2cnull mutants Notch-mediated signaling by Jag1 compensates for the loss of Jag2, preserving the balance of multiciliated vs. secretory cell differentiation
source: We also reasoned that in Jag2cnull mutants Notch-mediated signaling by Jag1 should compensate for the loss of Jag2, preserving the balance of multiciliated vs. secretory cell differentiation in these mutants. Indeed, analysis of Jag2cnull mice confirmed the presence of Jag1 signals in the intrapulmonary airway epithelium of these mutants (Figure 2D).
evidence: Based on in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2D and reasoning from expression patterns

claim: Double Jag1cnull; Jag2cnull mutants revealed an expansion in the population of basal progenitors
source: IF staining of Krt5 and β-tubulin in E18.5 Jag1cnull; Jag2cnull double mutants revealed an expansion in the population of basal progenitors and a variable but also increased population of multiciliated cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Based on immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A

claim: Double Jag1cnull; Jag2cnull mutants showed a variable but increased population of multiciliated cells
source: IF staining of Krt5 and β-tubulin in E18.5 Jag1cnull; Jag2cnull double mutants revealed an expansion in the population of basal progenitors and a variable but also increased population of multiciliated cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Based on immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A

claim: Jag2cnull tracheas had a significant increase in the number of prebasal cells
source: This analysis revealed that Jag2cnull tracheas had a significant increase in the number of prebasal cells (%p63+/DAPI) but a trend (not significant) towards an increase in the abundance of the multiciliated cell population (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: Based on morphometric analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B,C

claim: Jag2cnull tracheas showed a trend (not significant) towards an increase in the abundance of the multiciliated cell population
source: This analysis revealed that Jag2cnull tracheas had a significant increase in the number of prebasal cells (%p63+/DAPI) but a trend (not significant) towards an increase in the abundance of the multiciliated cell population (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: Based on morphometric analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B,C

claim: Jag2 is present in prebasal cells of the developing trachea
source: Notably, double ISH/immunohistochemistry for Jag2/p63 in WT confirmed the presence of Jag2 in prebasal cells of the developing trachea (Figure 1—figure supplement 1; Mori et al., 2015).
evidence: Based on double ISH/immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and previous publication

claim: Single Jag1cnull tracheas had no detectable change in the number of basal cell progenitors compared to controls
source: As expected from the distinct spatial distribution of these Jag ligands, single Jag1cnull tracheas had no detectable change in the number of basal cell progenitors compared to controls.
evidence: Based on morphometric analysis of tracheal sections

claim: In extrapulmonary airways (trachea) Jag2 predominantly contributes to the balance of basal versus luminal cells while Jag1 controls abundance of multiciliated cells
source: Together these data suggest that Jag ligands mediate overlapping but distinct events along the respiratory tract epithelium. In extrapulmonary airways (trachea here) Jag2 predominantly contributes to the balance of basal versus luminal cells while Jag1 controls abundance of multiciliated cells.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from combined analysis of single and double Jag mutants in trachea

claim: In intrapulmonary airways Jag1 is the predominant ligand regulating the balance of multiciliated versus club cell fate with a lesser contribution of Jag2
source: By contrast, in intrapulmonary airways Jag1 is the predominant ligand regulating the balance of multiciliated versus club cell fate with a lesser contribution of Jag2.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from combined analysis of single and double Jag mutants in intrapulmonary airways

claim: qPCR analysis showed no difference in Ascl1 expression between controls and mutants in any of the Jag-deficient airways at E18.5
source: Thus, we compared levels of Ascl1 expression in homogenates of Jag-cnull mutant lungs at E18.5, when NEBs are already widely distributed at branch point and internodal locations. qPCR analysis showed no difference in Ascl1 expression between controls and mutants in any of the Jag-deficient airways (Figure 3A).
evidence: Based on qPCR analysis shown in Figure 3A

claim: Immunofluorescence for Cgrp did not reveal consistent differences in expression patterns suggestive of alterations in NEBs' spatial distribution, size or frequency in intrapulmonary airways of Jag mutants compared to controls
source: Consistent with this, immunofluorescence for Cgrp, another established marker of PNEC fate (Li and Linnoila, 2012), did not reveal consistent differences in expression patterns, suggestive of alterations in NEBs' spatial distribution, size (~8–10 PNECs per NEB control, Jag1cnull, Jag2cnull, and double Jag1cnull; Jag2cnull) or frequency in intrapulmonary airways of mutants compared to controls (Figure 3A–D).
evidence: Based on immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3A-D and quantification

claim: NEBs contain approximately 8-10 PNECs per NEB in control, Jag1cnull, Jag2cnull, and double Jag1cnull; Jag2cnull mutants
source: Consistent with this, immunofluorescence for Cgrp, another established marker of PNEC fate (Li and Linnoila, 2012), did not reveal consistent differences in expression patterns, suggestive of alterations in NEBs' spatial distribution, size (~8–10 PNECs per NEB control, Jag1cnull, Jag2cnull, and double Jag1cnull; Jag2cnull) or frequency in intrapulmonary airways of mutants compared to controls (Figure 3A–D).
evidence: Based on quantification of immunofluorescence data

claim: Jag-mediated Notch signaling is unlikely to be involved in the mechanisms that initiate or restrict the domains of NEB or PNEC fate
source: Since in our mutants Jag is deleted well before epithelial progenitors differentiate, we concluded that Jag-mediated Notch signaling is unlikely to be involved in the mechanisms that initiate or restrict the domains of NEB or PNEC fate.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from the lack of NEB phenotype in Jag mutants

claim: Neither NEBs nor PNECs could be identified in extrapulmonary airways (trachea) of mutants or control animals
source: Neither NEBs nor PNECs could be identified in extrapulmonary airways (trachea) of mutants or control animals.
evidence: Based on examination of tracheal sections

claim: Strong N1ICD signals were found selectively in the SSEA1+ NEB-associated cell populations of double Jag1cnull; Jag2cnull mutants, indistinguishable from controls
source: Strong N1ICD labeling was found selectively in the SSEA1+ NEB-associated cell populations of mutants, indistinguishable from controls (Figure 3D).
evidence: Based on N1ICD immunofluorescence shown in Figure 3D

claim: qPCR analysis of Upk3a showed markedly decreased levels of expression in double Jag1cnull; Jag2cnull lungs
source: Lastly, qPCR analysis of Upk3a, a gene marker highly enriched in NEB-associated secretory cells but that also labels scattered secretory cells of intrapulmonary airways, showed markedly decreased levels of expression in double Jag1cnull; Jag2cnull lungs (Figure 3E).
evidence: Based on qPCR analysis shown in Figure 3E

claim: The NEB size and frequency in airways is not dependent on Jag ligands
source: The similar levels of Ascl1 and the Cgrp expression pattern we found in controls and double Jag mutants (Figure 3A) suggested that the NEB size and frequency in airways is not dependent on Jag ligands.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from comparison of Ascl1 and Cgrp expression between controls and mutants

claim: The remaining population of Upk3a-expressing cells in Jag1cnull; Jag2cnull mutants is associated with NEBs
source: Thus we reasoned that the remaining population of Upk3a-expressing cells in Jag1cnull; Jag2cnull mutants was associated with NEBs and that the significant decrease in Upk3a seen by qPCR resulted from the loss of the Upk3a-expressing scattered cell population. Indeed, ISH of Upk3a in these mutants showed signals restricted to branch points in proximal regions of intrapulmonary airways associated with Ascl1-expressing NEBs (Figure 3F).
evidence: Based on in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 3F and reasoning from qPCR results

claim: Jag1 and Jag2 have overlapping but also distinct roles in the cell fate specification of respiratory lineages in extrapulmonary and intrapulmonary airways
source: Together these results suggested that Jag1 and Jag2 have overlapping but also distinct roles in the cell fate specification of respiratory lineages in extrapulmonary and intrapulmonary airways.
evidence: Summary conclusion drawn from all Jag mutant analyses

claim: Jag ligands appear to be dispensable for activation of Notch and induction of NEB-associated secretory cells since they can utilize Dll provided by their neighboring NE cells
source: Jag ligands, however, appear to be dispensable for activation of Notch and induction of NEB-associated secretory cells since they can utilize Dll provided by their neighboring NE cells.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from the preserved NEB-associated secretory cells in Jag double mutants

claim: Jag ligands have no impact in regulating size or frequency of NEBs
source: Moreover, our data show no evidence that Jag ligands have any impact in regulating size or frequency of NEBs.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from the lack of NEB size or frequency changes in Jag mutants

claim: Dll1cnull; Dll4cnull E14.5 lungs showed a striking expansion in the population of Ascl1+ cells
source: IF analysis of E14.5 lungs from control mice showed the solitary PNECs and distinct small clusters of Ascl1+ cells in the epithelium of large intrapulmonary airways (bronchi) characteristic of the NEBs. By contrast, Dll1cnull; Dll4cnull E14.5 showed a striking expansion in the population of Ascl1+ cells (Figure 4A).
evidence: Based on immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4A

claim: In Dll1cnull; Dll4cnull mutants, individual Ascl1+ cell clusters could still be identified but they often seem to coalesce in large patches to form a nearly continuous layer of Ascl1+ cells
source: Although individual Ascl1+ cell clusters could still be identified, they often seem to coalesce in large patches to form a nearly continuous layer of Ascl1+ cells.
evidence: Based on immunofluorescence observations in Figure 4A

claim: In Dll1cnull; Dll4cnull mutants, Ascl1+ cells were not found ectopically in extrapulmonary airways or in the most distal airways undergoing branching morphogenesis
source: In spite of the distribution in wider domains, these cells were not found ectopically in extrapulmonary airways or in the most distal airways undergoing branching morphogenesis.
evidence: Based on examination of Ascl1+ cell distribution in mutants

claim: The large patches of Ascl1+ cells in Dll1cnull; Dll4cnull mutants were identified at branch points in E18.5 lungs and co-expressed Cgrp, indicating their continued differentiation
source: The large patches of Ascl1+ cells were identified at branch points in E18.5 lungs and by then co-expressed Cgrp, indicating their continued differentiation (Figure 4B).
evidence: Based on immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4B

claim: Loss of Dll ligands expanded the Ascl1+ pool of PNEC/NEB precursors and did not prevent these cells from initiating maturation
source: Thus, loss of Dll ligands expanded the Ascl1+ pool of PNEC/NEB precursors and did not prevent these cells from initiating maturation.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from Ascl1 and Cgrp co-expression in expanded cell populations

claim: Ki67 staining showed no difference in labeling associated with the Ascl1-expressing cells between control and double Dll mutants at E18.5 or E14.5
source: Interestingly, Ki67 staining showed no difference in labeling associated with the Ascl1-expressing cells between control and double mutants at E18.5 or E14.5 (Figure 4C).
evidence: Based on Ki67 immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4C

claim: The NEB expansion found in Dll1cnull; Dll4cnull mutants did not result from an increase in proliferation
source: The data supported the idea that the NEB expansion found in Dll1cnull; Dll4cnull mutants did not result from an increase in proliferation.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from Ki67 staining results

claim: Double Dll1cnull; Dll4cnull mutants showed a significant increase in Ascl1 expression compared to controls
source: Double Dll mutants showed a significant increase in these transcripts compared to controls (Ascl1 p=1.1×10−6; Cgrp p=5.9×10−5), consistent with the aberrant NE cell expansion.
evidence: Based on qPCR analysis shown in Figure 4D

claim: Double Dll1cnull; Dll4cnull mutants showed a significant increase in Cgrp expression compared to controls
source: Double Dll mutants showed a significant increase in these transcripts compared to controls (Ascl1 p=1.1×10−6; Cgrp p=5.9×10−5), consistent with the aberrant NE cell expansion.
evidence: Based on qPCR analysis shown in Figure 4D

claim: In single Dll1cnull lungs Ascl1 expression was modestly increased
source: However, in single Dll1cnull or Dll4cnull lungs Ascl1 expression was modestly increased only in Dll1cnull and Cgrp mRNA was not altered in either of these mutants compared to controls.
evidence: Based on qPCR analysis shown in Figure 4D

claim: Cgrp mRNA was not altered in single Dll1cnull or Dll4cnull mutants compared to controls
source: However, in single Dll1cnull or Dll4cnull lungs Ascl1 expression was modestly increased only in Dll1cnull and Cgrp mRNA was not altered in either of these mutants compared to controls.
evidence: Based on qPCR analysis shown in Figure 4D

claim: The marked difference in phenotype between double and single Dll mutants suggests functional redundancy between Dll1 and Dll4 in controlling NEB or PNEC-associated events
source: The marked difference in phenotype between double and single Dll mutants suggested functional redundancy between Dll1 and Dll4 in controlling NEB or PNEC-associated events.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from comparing phenotypes of single and double Dll mutants

claim: Quantitation of the number of solitary PNECs in the airway epithelium showed no difference between controls and any of the single or double Dll mutants
source: Quantitation of the number of solitary PNECs in the airway epithelium showed no difference between controls and any of the single or double mutants, suggesting that Dll disruption affected primarily the NEB microenvironment.
evidence: Based on morphometric analysis shown in Figure 4E

claim: Dll disruption affected primarily the NEB microenvironment
source: Quantitation of the number of solitary PNECs in the airway epithelium showed no difference between controls and any of the single or double mutants, suggesting that Dll disruption affected primarily the NEB microenvironment.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from the lack of change in solitary PNECs

claim: The frequency of NEBs per airway was largely unaffected in Dll mutants, although a small difference in Dll4 mutants reached statistical significance
source: The frequency of NEBs per airway (%) was largely unaffected, although a small difference in Dll4 mutants reached statistical significance.
evidence: Based on morphometric analysis shown in Figure 4E

claim: The number of PNECs per NEB was significantly increased in both the Dll1cnull; Dll4cnull and single Dll4cnull airways
source: However, the number of PNECs per NEB was significantly increased in both the Dll1cnull; Dll4cnull and single Dll4cnull airways, indicating that the size of NEBs was dramatically altered in these mutants.
evidence: Based on morphometric analysis shown in Figure 4E

claim: The size of NEBs was dramatically altered in Dll1cnull; Dll4cnull and Dll4cnull mutants
source: However, the number of PNECs per NEB was significantly increased in both the Dll1cnull; Dll4cnull and single Dll4cnull airways, indicating that the size of NEBs was dramatically altered in these mutants.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from the increased number of PNECs per NEB

claim: The mechanisms that restrict PNEC fate and limit expansion of NEB were severely disrupted in Dll mutants
source: Together the data indicated that the mechanisms that restrict PNEC fate and limit expansion of NEB were severely disrupted in Dll mutants.
evidence: Summary conclusion drawn from all Dll mutant analyses

claim: Strong N1ICD signals were found in the NE-associated CCs of Dll1cnull; Dll4cnull mutants indistinguishable from that of controls
source: Double IF for Ascl1 and N1ICD in E18.5 lung sections showed strong N1ICD signals in the NE-associated CCs of mutants indistinguishable from that of controls (Figure 5A).
evidence: Based on immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5A

claim: The NEB expansion in Dll1cnull; Dll4cnull mutants was accompanied by a respective expansion of the NEB-associated CCs
source: Notably, the NEB expansion in Dll1cnull; Dll4cnull mutants was accompanied by a respective expansion of the NEB-associated CCs.
evidence: Based on immunofluorescence observations in Figure 5A

claim: NEB-associated cells show characteristic low levels of Cyp2f2 expression in contrast to the strong signals outside the NEB microenvironment
source: Double ISH/immunohistochemistry showed the characteristic low levels of Cyp2f2 expression in NEB-associated cells in contrast to the strong signals outside the NEB microenvironment (Figure 5B).
evidence: Based on double ISH/immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 5B

claim: qPCR analysis showed a significant increase in expression of Upk3a in Dll1cnull; Dll4cnull mutants compared to controls
source: The aberrant expansion of the NEB-associated cells was further demonstrated by qPCR analysis of lung homogenates, which showed a significant increase in expression of Upk3a in Dll1cnull; Dll4cnull mutants compared to controls (Figure 6A).
evidence: Based on qPCR analysis shown in Figure 6A

claim: No change in expression of Scgb1a1 (CC10) or Foxj1 was found in Dll1cnull; Dll4cnull mutants
source: Of note, we found no change in expression of markers not directly associated with the NEB microenvironment, such as Scgb1a1 (CC10) or Foxj1, which suggested that the Jag ligands present in double Dll1cnull; Dll4cnull lungs were capable of activating Notch and mediating the balance of secretory-ciliated cell differentiation (Figure 6A).
evidence: Based on qPCR analysis shown in Figure 6A

claim: The Jag ligands present in double Dll1cnull; Dll4cnull lungs are capable of activating Notch and mediating the balance of secretory-ciliated cell differentiation
source: Of note, we found no change in expression of markers not directly associated with the NEB microenvironment, such as Scgb1a1 (CC10) or Foxj1, which suggested that the Jag ligands present in double Dll1cnull; Dll4cnull lungs were capable of activating Notch and mediating the balance of secretory-ciliated cell differentiation (Figure 6A).
evidence: Conclusion drawn from the lack of change in Scgb1a1 and Foxj1 expression

claim: ISH confirmed the marked expansion in the domain of expression of Upk3a in Dll1cnull; Dll4cnull mice and their association with NEBs
source: Lastly, ISH of E18.5 lungs confirmed the marked expansion in the domain of expression of Upk3a in Dll1cnull; Dll4cnull mice and their association with NEBs (Figure 6B–C).
evidence: Based on in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 6B-C

claim: In spite of the inability to express Dll1 and Dll4, key features of the NEB microenvironment are preserved in Dll1cnull; Dll4cnull mutants by Jag ligand activation of Notch signaling
source: Together the data strongly suggested that, in spite of the inability to express Dll1 and Dll4, key features of the NEB microenvironment are preserved in these mutants by Jag ligand activation of Notch signaling.
evidence: Summary conclusion drawn from all observations in Dll double mutants

claim: Jagged-driven Notch signaling differentially regulates cell type-specific programs of cell fate in a temporal and spatial fashion along the developing respiratory tract epithelium
source: Here we provide evidence for distinct roles of Notch ligands once epithelial progenitors initiate differentiation. We show that Jagged-driven Notch signaling differentially regulates cell type-specific programs of cell fate in a temporal and spatial fashion along the developing respiratory tract epithelium.
evidence: Summary statement of main findings

claim: Jag ligands are not required to induce or maintain the fate of basal cell precursors in extrapulmonary airways
source: In extrapulmonary airways (largely trachea here) we found that Jag ligands are not required to induce or maintain the fate of basal cell precursors.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from analysis of basal cells in Jag mutants

claim: Double Jag1 and Jag2 deletion leads to a major imbalance between the basal and luminal compartments with an expansion of basal cell precursors
source: These precursors are known to generate luminal cells in fetal airways (Yang et al., 2018) and we now report that double Jag1 and Jag2 deletion leads to a major imbalance between the basal and luminal compartments with an expansion of basal cell precursors.
evidence: Based on morphometric analysis of basal cells in double Jag mutants with reference to previous work

claim: Loss of both Jag ligands in intrapulmonary airways had no detectable impact on the NEB microenvironment
source: By contrast, loss of both Jag ligands in intrapulmonary airways had no detectable impact on the NEB microenvironment.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from analysis of NEBs in Jag double mutants

claim: Dll inactivation in Dll1cnull; Dll4cnull mutants resulted in marked expansion of NEBs and their associated secretory cells
source: Unexpectedly, we found that Dll inactivation in Dll1cnull; Dll4cnull mutants resulted in marked expansion of NEBs and their associated secretory cells.
evidence: Summary of main finding from Dll mutant analysis

claim: Although Ascl1-labeled NE precursors have been reported in the embryonic lung as early as E12.5, no expression of Dll (or Jag) ligands by these cells was found prior to E13.5
source: Interestingly, although Ascl1-labeled NE precursors have been reported in the embryonic lung as early as E12.5, we found no expression of Dll (or Jag) ligands by these cells prior to E13.5 (Figure 1; Beckers et al., 1999; Post et al., 2000; Li and Linnoila, 2012; Kuo and Krasnow, 2015).
evidence: Based on in situ hybridization data with reference to previous publications

claim: There is evidence that Hes1 is expressed and already active early in the developing lung epithelium in spite of no evidence of ligand expression in intrapulmonary airways to activate Notch signaling nearby NE cells
source: This was intriguing since there is evidence that Hes1 is expressed and already active early in the developing lung epithelium in spite of no evidence of ligand expression in intrapulmonary airways to activate Notch signaling nearby NE cells (Tsao et al., 2009; Noguchi et al., 2015).
evidence: Based on previous publications cited

claim: At initial stages NE vs. non-NE cell fate selection is mediated by Hes1 in a Notch-independent fashion
source: This suggests that at these initial stages NE vs. non-NE cell fate selection is mediated by Hes1 in a Notch-independent fashion.
evidence: Inference drawn from the lack of ligand expression but presence of Hes1 activity

claim: Hes1 deletion in lung epithelial progenitors at the onset of lung development results in aberrant expansion of NEB precursors as early as E13.5
source: Consistent with this, Hes1 deletion in lung epithelial progenitors at the onset of lung development (Shhcre/+; Hes1flox/flox) results in aberrant expansion of NEB precursors as early as E13.5 (Noguchi et al., 2015).
evidence: Based on previous publication cited

claim: Hes1-dependency on Notch is likely established at later developmental stages
source: Hes1-dependency on Notch is likely established at later developmental stages and could explain why genetic inactivation of the key Notch pathway components Pofut1 or Rbpjk using the ShhCre driver (the same used to delete Hes1, above), had no apparent effect in NE abundance at early (E14.5) stages compared to the severe effects at later (E18.5) stages (Tsao et al., 2009) and not shown).
evidence: Inference drawn from comparing timing of phenotypes in different mutants with reference to previous work

claim: Dll1cnull; Dll4cnull mutants provide the first genetic proof that these ligands are crucially involved in regulating the size of NEBs
source: Our Dll1cnull; Dll4cnull mutants provided the first genetic proof that these ligands are crucially involved in regulating the size the NEBs, with no clear role in controlling other aspects such as the number of PNECs or NEBs per airway.
evidence: Summary of novel finding from Dll mutant analysis

claim: Dll ligands have no clear role in controlling the number of PNECs or NEBs per airway
source: Our Dll1cnull; Dll4cnull mutants provided the first genetic proof that these ligands are crucially involved in regulating the size the NEBs, with no clear role in controlling other aspects such as the number of PNECs or NEBs per airway.
evidence: Based on morphometric analysis of Dll mutants

claim: Jag ligands have no detectable influence in NEB size or abundance
source: By contrast, Jag ligands had no detectable influence in NEB size or abundance.
evidence: Based on analysis of NEBs in Jag mutants

claim: At E14.5, when NEBs are forming along the proximal-distal axis of intrapulmonary airways, Jag2 is still strongly expressed only at partially overlapping proximal domains such that nascent distal clusters of Ascl1+ cells arise in non-Jag2 or non-Jag1-expressing areas
source: Even at E14.5, when NEBs are forming along the proximal-distal axis of intrapulmonary airways, Jag2 is still strongly expressed only at partially overlapping proximal domains such that nascent distal clusters of Ascl1+ cells arise in non-Jag2 or non-Jag1-expressing areas (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Based on in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2

claim: A wave of Jag-Notch activation initiating in the trachea progresses in a proximal-distal fashion to establish the balance of secretory vs. multiciliated cell fates in intrapulmonary airways
source: Together our data suggest a model for the role of Notch ligands in lung development (Figure 7) in which early, when epithelial progenitors start to differentiate, a wave of Jag-Notch activation initiating in the trachea progresses in a proximal-distal fashion to establish the balance of secretory vs. multiciliated cell fates in intrapulmonary airways.
evidence: Model proposed based on integration of all findings

claim: As NEBs start to express Dll ligands, Dll-Notch signaling is turned on in adjacent cells to form NEB-associated CCs
source: A program of NE cell fate also emerges in intrapulmonary airways and as NEB start to express Dll ligands, Dll-Notch signaling is turned on in adjacent cells to form NEB-associated CCs.
evidence: Model proposed based on integration of findings

claim: Local activation of Notch signaling in NEB-associated cells shelters the NEB microenvironment from the neighboring epithelium, preventing aberrant NEB expansion
source: Local activation of Notch signaling in these cells shelters the NEB microenvironment from the neighboring epithelium, preventing aberrant NEB expansion.
evidence: Model proposed based on the NEB expansion phenotype in Dll mutants

claim: The role of preventing aberrant NEB expansion is restricted to Dll1 and Dll4
source: This role is restricted to Dll1 and Dll4, given that Jag1, Jag2 single or double mutants showed no detectable effect in the size of NEBs, NEB-associated CCs or local Notch activation.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from comparing Jag and Dll mutant phenotypes

claim: The NEB microenvironment is maintained by Dll ligands that induce Notch to maintain the local balance of NE and non-NE cell types
source: The NEB microenvironment is maintained by Dll ligands that induce Notch to maintain the local balance of NE and non-NE cell types.
evidence: Model proposed based on findings

claim: The relevance of a late Notch-dependent phase is underscored by the expansion of the NE domain when Dll ligands are unavailable to induce Notch to generate NE-associated CCs locally
source: The relevance of a late Notch-dependent phase is underscored by the expansion of the NE domain when Dll ligands are unavailable to induce Notch to generate NE-associated CCs locally.
evidence: Interpretation of the Dll mutant phenotype

claim: The cell fate specification events described precede or overlap at least partially with migratory and cluster-forming events of NEBs
source: Our observations are not in conflict with recent reports that describe aggregation of NEB by a mechanism of NE cell migration (slithering) (Kuo and Krasnow, 2015; Noguchi et al., 2015; Branchfield et al., 2016). Rather we envision that the cell fate specification events described above precede these migratory and cluster-forming events, or overlap at least partially with mechanisms reported here.
evidence: Interpretation of findings in context of previous publications

claim: In spite of the absence of Dll ligands and having Jag1 and Jag2 as the sole ligands available, the NEB-associated CC in Dll1cnull; Dll4cnull airways exhibited robust Notch activation and maintained the unique features of CCs in this microenvironment
source: Intriguingly, in spite of the absence of Dll ligands and having Jag1 and Jag2 as the sole ligands available, the NEB-associated CC in Dll1cnull; Dll4cnull airways exhibited robust Notch activation and maintained the unique features of CCs in this microenvironment (strong Upk3a, SSEA1, and low Cyp2f2).
evidence: Based on analysis of NEB-associated cells in Dll double mutants

claim: The unique features of NEB-associated CCs (strong Upk3a, SSEA1, and low Cyp2f2) do not necessarily depend on the differential activation of Notch by NE-derived Dll ligands and can result from Jag-Notch activation in the cells immediately adjacent to NEBs
source: This suggested that the features above do not necessarily depend on the differential activation of Notch by NE-derived Dll ligands and can result from Jag-Notch activation in the cells immediately adjacent to NEBs.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from the preserved NEB-associated CC features in Dll mutants

claim: A currently unidentified cell membrane-associated component of NE cells or a short-range diffusible signal(s) emanating from NEBs may modulate Notch signaling or influence the cell fate program in adjacent CCs to endow unique features
source: We speculate that a currently unidentified cell membrane-associated component of NE cells or a short-range diffusible signal(s) emanating from NEBs modulates Notch signaling or influences the cell fate program in adjacent CCs to endow these features (Figure 7).
evidence: Speculation based on the preserved features of NEB-associated CCs in Dll mutants

claim: Mass spectrometric analysis has demonstrated Lfng to promote Notch activation by Dll1 and decrease its activation by Jag1
source: Mass spectrometric analysis has demonstrated Lfng to promote Notch activation by Dll1 and decrease its activation by Jag1 (Kakuda and Haltiwanger, 2017).
evidence: Based on previous publication cited

claim: Lfng is expressed in NEBs rather than in the NEB-associated CCs, which activates Notch signaling
source: Lfng is expressed in NEBs rather than in the NEB-associated CCs, which activates Notch signaling (Xu et al., 2010b; Xu et al., 2010a).
evidence: Based on previous publications cited

claim: In the developing intestinal epithelium Fringe is expressed in the ligand-presenting cells to promote Notch activity in the neighboring cells
source: This is reminiscent of the developing intestinal epithelium where Fringe is expressed in the ligand-presenting cells to promote Notch activity in the neighboring cells (Kadur Lakshminarasimha Murthy et al., 2018).
evidence: Based on previous publication cited

claim: There is currently no evidence that Fringe proteins influence epithelial Notch signaling in the developing lung epithelium
source: There is currently no evidence that these proteins influence epithelial Notch signaling in the developing lung epithelium (van Tuyl et al., 2005; Xu et al., 2010b; Xu et al., 2010a).
evidence: Based on previous publications cited

claim: Analysis of human biopsies from normal donors and patients with pulmonary NE cell hyperplasias suggest that both the NE and NE-associated CC components are coordinately altered
source: Indeed, analysis of human biopsies from normal donors and patients with pulmonary NE cell hyperplasias suggest that both the NE and NE-associated CC components are coordinately altered (Guha et al., 2017).
evidence: Based on previous publication cited

claim: These mechanisms may potentially play a role in human conditions that result in aberrant NE differentiation, including NE hyperplasias and cancer
source: These mechanisms may potentially play a role in human conditions that result in aberrant NE differentiation, including NE hyperplasias and cancer.
evidence: Speculation about potential clinical relevance

claim: In mammals, four Notch receptors (Notch1–4) and five ligands (Delta-like: Dll1, Dll3 and Dll4 and Jagged: Jag1 and Jag2) have been described
source: In mammals, four Notch receptors (Notch1–4) and five ligands (Delta-like: Dll1, Dll3 and Dll4 and Jagged: Jag1 and Jag2) have been described.
evidence: Statement of established knowledge

claim: All Notch ligands, except Dll3, are Notch activating
source: All ligands, except Dll3, are Notch activating.
evidence: Statement of established knowledge

claim: Signaling is triggered by ligand-receptor binding through cell-cell interactions, which leads to sequential cleavage of the Notch receptor and binding of its intracellular domain (NICD) to a CSL/RBPJk-activator complex for activation of downstream target genes, such as HEY/HES-family members
source: Signaling is triggered by ligand-receptor binding through cell-cell interactions, which leads to sequential cleavage of the Notch receptor and binding of its intracellular domain (NICD) to a CSL/RBPJk-activator complex for activation of downstream target genes, such as HEY/HES-family members (Radtke and Raj, 2003; Bray, 2006).
evidence: Statement of established knowledge with citations

claim: Evidence from genetic studies suggest that the Notch effects are not necessarily dependent on the type of NICD but rather of NICD dosage
source: While different Notch receptors are known to act in a variety of biological processes, evidence from genetic studies suggest that the Notch effects are not necessarily dependent on the type of NICD but rather of NICD dosage (Liu et al., 2015).
evidence: Based on previous publication cited

claim: Specific Notch ligand-receptor binding in mammalian cells appears to be mostly non-selective or context-dependent
source: Notably, specific Notch ligand-receptor binding in mammalian cells appears to be mostly non-selective or context-dependent.
evidence: Statement of current understanding

claim: Systemic deletion of Jag1, Jag2, or Dll4 has been shown to result in distinct phenotypes, suggesting that these ligands could mediate unique functions not entirely due to the receptor they activate
source: Interestingly, systemic deletion of Jag1, Jag2, or Dll4 has been shown to result in distinct phenotypes, suggesting that these ligands could mediate unique functions not entirely due to the receptor they activate (D'Souza et al., 2009; Choi et al., 2009).
evidence: Based on previous publications cited

claim: Notch ligands were reported to activate distinct targets even through binding to the same Notch receptor and ligand-specific effects have been observed in multiple contexts
source: Indeed, Notch ligands were reported to activate distinct targets even through binding to the same Notch receptor and ligand-specific effects have been observed in multiple contexts (Nandagopal et al., 2018).
evidence: Based on previous publication cited

claim: When airways are still forming epithelial progenitors initiate a differentiation program that gives rise to secretory (club, goblet), multiciliated, and neuroendocrine (NE) cells
source: When airways are still forming epithelial progenitors initiate a differentiation program that gives rise to secretory (club, goblet), multiciliated, and neuroendocrine (NE) cells.
evidence: Statement of established knowledge

claim: Disruption of Rbpjk or the o-fucosyl-transferase Pofut1 required for Notch signaling results in aberrant expansion of multiciliated and NE cells at the cost of secretory cells
source: Disruption of Rbpjk or the o-fucosyl-transferase Pofut1 required for Notch signaling results in aberrant expansion of multiciliated and NE cells at the cost of secretory cells (Tsao et al., 2009; Tsao et al., 2011; Morimoto et al., 2010).
evidence: Based on previous publications cited

claim: Club cells are more sensitive to deficiency in Notch2 while Notch 1-3 receptors contribute to control the NE population in an additive manner
source: Subsequent studies showed that club cells are more sensitive to deficiency in Notch2 while Notch 1-3 receptors contribute to control the NE population in an additive manner (Morimoto et al., 2012).
evidence: Based on previous publication cited

claim: Notch ligands (Dll1, Dll4, Jag1, and Jag2) have been reported in partially overlapping but also distinct domains in the lung
source: Notably, these ligands have been reported in partially overlapping but also distinct domains in the lung (Post et al., 2000; Kong et al., 2004; Tsao et al., 2009; Xu et al., 2010b; Zhang et al., 2013; Mori et al., 2015).
evidence: Based on previous publications cited

claim: Inactivation of Jag1 in epithelial progenitors of intrapulmonary airways undergoing branching morphogenesis using a surfactant protein-c (Sftpc)-tet-O system was shown to disrupt epithelial differentiation
source: Inactivation of Jag1 in epithelial progenitors of intrapulmonary airways undergoing branching morphogenesis using a surfactant protein-c (Sftpc)-tet-O system was shown to disrupt epithelial differentiation (Zhang et al., 2013), confirming the previously reported role of Notch signaling in this process (Tsao et al., 2009; Morimoto et al., 2010).
evidence: Based on previous publications cited

claim: Jag2 systemic knockout animals die at birth
source: Jag2 systemic knockout animals die at birth (Jiang et al., 1998).
evidence: Based on previous publication cited

claim: Gross morphological analysis of the Jag mutant lungs showed no notable macroscopic difference in size or shape
source: Gross morphological analysis of the mutant lungs showed no notable macroscopic difference in size or shape (not shown).
evidence: Based on observation of mutant lungs
